title: Jerk Chicken
subtitle: Jamaican spiced and grilled chicken with scotch bonnet and allspice
excerpt: The definitive Jamaican preparation: chicken marinated overnight in a fiery paste of scotch bonnet, allspice, thyme, garlic, and ginger, then cooked over high heat until charred and smoky on the outside and juicy within. The marinade is the dish.

recipe.sourceNotes: Jerk cooking is a method of cooking meat — originally pork, now most commonly chicken — developed by the Maroon communities of Jamaica, drawing on techniques brought by enslaved Africans combined with Arawak indigenous smoking and spicing traditions. The word jerk derives from the Spanish charqui (dried meat) or from a Peruvian Quechua word for dried meat. Allspice (pimento in Jamaica) is the signature spice; scotch bonnet provides the heat. Authentic jerk is cooked over pimento wood, which is unavailable outside Jamaica and some specialist Caribbean suppliers, but charcoal grilling provides a reasonable approximation. Oven-baked jerk chicken, while acceptable, lacks the smoke and char that define the dish. The overnight marinade is not optional: the spices must penetrate the flesh to give the result its depth.

content.text: Marinate overnight, or for 24 hours if possible. Score the chicken deeply (to the bone on drumsticks) so the marinade penetrates. Use gloves when handling scotch bonnets; the capsaicin oil is intensely irritating and hard to remove. The char on the outside is deliberate and desirable: jerk chicken should be blackened in places.

items.preparation: bone-in, skin-on; scored deeply through the skin
1–3 depending on heat tolerance; deseeded for less heat

content.text: Blend all the marinade ingredients (scotch bonnets through salt) together in a blender or food processor until a smooth, thick paste. Taste and adjust the heat, salt, and sweetness. Pour over the scored chicken pieces, working the paste into the cuts. Cover and refrigerate overnight, or for at least 4 hours.

To cook on a barbecue: cook over medium-high direct heat, turning frequently, for 30 to 40 minutes until charred and cooked through. To cook in the oven: heat to 220 C (200 C fan). Place the chicken on a rack over a roasting tin and roast for 40 to 45 minutes, turning halfway, until the skin is charred and the juices run clear.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving. Serve with rice and peas and fried plantain.
